$comment: WordRoots textbook registry. One entry per source the curriculum is derived from. `status` is deliberately blunt: a source is never marked complete unless its full text was actually parsed in this workspace.

sources.title: English Vocabulary Elements
sources.evidence: EPUB parsed locally: 11 chapters + 2 appendices + glossary; appendix element table transcribed page by page (analysis/s1/appendix).
sources.rights: User-provided copy. Not redistributed: no EPUB, no scanned pages, no verbatim prose in this repository. Only derived facts (element forms, glosses, chapter references) and original Chinese explanations are stored.

sources.title: Essentials of Linguistics
sources.evidence: Pressbooks WXR export parsed locally (5.1 MB); EPUB/PDF kept for page-level checks. Morphology, Semantics and Historical Linguistics extracted into s2-topics.json (141 knowledge points) and glossary-s2.json.
sources.note: Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: attribution and share-alike apply to adapted teaching text. The repository stores only original Chinese explanations and facts, never the book text.

sources.title: WordWorks Structured Word Inquiry resources
sources.evidence: 5 PDFs parsed locally (Bowers & Kirby 2010, two handouts, workshop booklet, spelling-out paper). Extracted 14 practices with page-level provenance into s3-method.json.
sources.note: Author-copyrighted handouts, publicly downloadable but not redistributable. Only the method (four questions, word sum, matrix) is re-expressed in original Chinese; no handout text or scan is committed.
sources.rights: Author-copyrighted handouts and papers (Bowers & Kirby 2010, workshop booklet, spelling-out paper). Not redistributed: only the method is described, no PDF pages, no verbatim prose.

sources.title: New Word-Analysis
sources.author: William Swinton
sources.evidence: Project Gutenberg #19346 text parsed locally: 608 element entries extracted into s4-elements.json; 197 overlap S1, 18 conflict, 7 marked obsolete after modern-etymology checks.
sources.note: Public domain in the US. 1879 etymologies are re-checked against modern references; entries that no longer hold are flagged obsolete rather than silently taught.
sources.rights: Public domain (New Word-Analysis, 1879). Quoted only for historical framing; no facsimile pages shipped.

sources.title: Historical and etymological references (reference set)
sources.evidence: Cited per word for Indo-European and Latin/Greek etymology. Members: Oxford English Dictionary (3rd ed., etymology sections), Online Etymology Dictionary, Lewis & Short Latin Dictionary, Liddell-Scott-Jones Greek Lexicon, Wiktionary etymology sections.
sources.rights: Consulted for facts only. No text reproduced.
sources.citationPolicy: A citation must name the specific entry, e.g. {id:'S5', detail:'OED 3e, s.v. religion, etymology'}. A bare 'S5' with no detail is recorded as an unlocated citation and cannot alone justify etymology.status='documented'.

sources.title: English gloss / definition reference
sources.evidence: Used for modern English senses and register labels (e.g. Merriam-Webster, Cambridge, Wiktionary senses).
sources.rights: Licensed reference works consulted for facts only. Not redistributed: no entries, definitions or article text are shipped; citations point at the work, not at copied content.
sources.citationPolicy: A citation must name the entry and sense, e.g. {id:'G1', detail:'MW, s.v. lucid, sense 1a'}.

sources.title: Internal lexical rules (project-defined)
sources.evidence: Orthographic rules of this project: silent-e loss, y→i, consonant doubling, assimilation sets. These are rules, not sources of linguistic fact.
sources.rights: Project original (MIT). Not a linguistic source: records our own analysis rules. Not an external reference.
sources.citationPolicy: Citing LEX means 'derived by a project rule', never 'verified by a dictionary'.

sources.title: A Latin Dictionary (Lewis & Short, founded on Andrews' edition of Freund's Latin dictionary)
sources.evidence: Full text retrieved from Internet Archive (2015.120891.A-Latin-Dictionary-Lewis-And-Short_djvu.txt, 679,635 lines); headword entries quoted with line numbers. The other Internet Archive scan (latindictionaryf00lewiiala) is the school abridgement and is NOT this source.
sources.rights: Public domain (1879). Quoted in short excerpts only for verification; the full text is not redistributed.
sources.note: Independent editorial source from Wiktionary: 19th-century Latin lexicography, useful for checking etymon and sense.
